analysis:
All three changed files are test-only under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. No production code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, or cache-storage behavior changes in this batch, so no security regression is evident.

1. MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineTests.swift adds gptOssStopStringsAreScopedToTheFinalChannel (head lines 625-634). It pins ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope for gpt-oss by model id and by model_type, and returns nil for gemma and qwen. This documents that the production scope logic exists; the implementation was not supplied. The test is a regression pin rather than new attack surface.

2. NativeBlockRetirementBridgeTests.swift adds a TextSession fixture (head lines 50-71) and nativeBlockRequestsCarryNoStopScope (head lines 94-116). The test asserts that the native-block engine matches stops over the whole output, ignores the reasoning scope, and reports the matched stop. Whether production code drops the scope on the native path was not reviewed, since the implementation is outside this batch. The test uses in-memory fixtures, and the KV budget and reservation accounting patterns are unchanged. This is relevant to T-010 and the T-041 resource-retirement context.

3. GemmaToolCallLiveTests.swift (head line 264) changes `.info` to `.info, .logprobs` in a switch. This implies a new `.logprobs` event case in the production stream enum. The enum definition and any logprobs emission were not supplied. Whether logprobs add a data-exposure or encryption path for A-001 (the T-008 fail-closed concern) cannot be assessed from this batch.

Follow-up for the integration pass: check the production logprobs event path and the stop-scope code to confirm that the logprobs response stays sealed to the consumer and is not emitted as plaintext.
